sentences.text:
Bihari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
 Cra No. 8960 of 2019
 (Bihari Vs The State Of Madhya Prade
 Dated : 06-11-2025

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Pradeep Kumar Naveria - Advocate for the appellan
 Shri Yash Soni - Public Prosecutor for the respondent/

Heard on I.A.No.21979 of 2025, which is the fourth application under Section 389(1) of
Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of Bnss,2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
His first application for temporary suspension of sentence and grant of bail vide order dated 17.06.2022 is dismissed since the date of marriage is already over.

Second application was dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 10.04.2023 and third application was disposed of with the direction of early hearing of the matter vide order dated 16.06.2023.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 27.09.2019 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Deori, District Sagar (M.P.) in S.T.No.219 of 2014, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction Imprisonment Fine In lieu of default fine U/s.
 450 of IPC R.I. for 05 years Rs.1,000/
 
 376(g) of IPC Life Imprisonment Rs.1,000/
 
With the direction that all sentences shall run concurrently.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Deori, District Sagar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the present appellant.
He further submits that appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The 2 CRA-8960-2019 victim is a major lady.
There were no injuries over the body of the prosecutrix, thus it is a case of consent.
It is further submitted that the other co-accused has already undergone the sentence imposed upon and is out of the jail.
Present appellant was absconding and surrendered later on, therefore, trial was conducted against him.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses.
Appellant is the first offender having no criminal past.
The appellant is in jail and has already undergone more than 06 years of incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2019 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.

Hence, it is prayed that the application for Bihari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137983333/
1 suspension of sentence may be allowed.

entities.text: Bihari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and appellant being the first offender having no criminal background, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended 3 CRA-8960-2019 and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 18.02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJAY KUMA  JUDGE JU  SSL Bihari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137983333/
